harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 to run a Python 2.4 web application in `/srv/chroot-web-app` as the non-login `appsvc` account. It listens on port 8080, starts through SysV init, and recovered successfully after a full node reboot. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the unprivileged system account `appsvc` with `/sbin/nologin`.
Created a root-owned chroot containing the application data.
Installed a legacy-compatible Python 2.4 launcher that enters the chroot and then drops to the `appsvc` UID/GID.
Installed and enabled the `chroot-web-app` SysV service.
Verified HTTP access through the managed node IP.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified boot persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside a chroot as appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: `/proc` identifies `/srv/chroot-web-app` as the process root, UID/GID 101/102 as appsvc, and PPID 1. Port 8080 listens on all interfaces and returns HTTP 200 with the expected chroot-resident content.

evidence.requirement: Starts at boot without an interactive login session
evidence.summary: SysV runlevel startup is enabled, appsvc uses `/sbin/nologin`, and the service automatically returned after reboot without a login session.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after configuration, node1 reports CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.

Healthy baseline boot ID was `e550e074-b6dd-410c-8000-000000000000`; the reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID is `53793130-b823-4d29-8000-000000000000`; post-restart evidence confirms recovered service, chroot, appsvc identity, listener, data, and HTTP response.
